pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound identifying a mature ovarian teratoma containing ectopic neural tissue, paired with positive anti-GluN1 antibodies in the CSF. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is a severe autoimmune condition often triggered as a paraneoplastic syndrome, most commonly by a benign ovarian teratoma containing nervous tissue. The host immune system generates antibodies against the ectopic neural cells expressing the GluN1 subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to neuronal NMDA receptors in the CNS, causing receptor cross-linking and internalisation. This leads to a progressive loss of NMDA receptor function, precipitating psychotic symptoms, memory deficits, involuntary movements, autonomic dysfunction, hypoventilation, and seizures. Removal of the tumor along with prompt immunotherapy leads to significant clinical improvement.
